## Close record — change 2002 merged

Merged as `1cb68ec230b1e50c10e3fdc0fdfebdaa9078fb66` on `main`. Gerrit rebased
on submit, so my local `cd8fdb4622` is NOT an ancestor of `origin/main`;
identity was confirmed the safe way rather than by diff:

- the merged commit carries my `Change-Id: I4cb4a11970750d594b3a81a5c651b87d08ba441e`
- blob SHA of `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` is `d98ac01313240431b6c87c96a57216e9a1bd97d5`
  in ALL THREE of my local commit, the merged commit, and the current
  `origin/main` tip — byte-identical, and not subsequently altered by the
  commits that landed after it

Field confirmation from the coordinator: the two changes still carrying the
skew (2001, 1998) both went green on their next run, and changes pushed since
are unaffected. Six changes had been reddened; the count stopped there.

## Acceptance criteria — all three met

AC1 and AC2 were verified directly by executing each step's `run:` block
verbatim against archived trees, in both directions (evidence table in the
previous comment).

AC3 carries a **recorded divergence**: it asks for verification against one of
1997/1998/1999 before their rebase, and those changes had already rebased or
landed by the time I fixed this. I satisfied it by equivalent reconstruction —
an archived pre-`02f71da097` tree exercising the identical `run:` block, which
skips instead of exiting 4. Noting rather than rewording: the AC's own text
admits "or an equivalent reconstruction", so this is within its terms, and the
post-merge behaviour of 2001/1998 has since supplied the direct evidence the
AC originally asked for.

## The change's main judgment call — separate guards, not a joint one

The first step invokes two scripts with a five-week vintage gap:

| script | added by | date |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` | `8c29eca552` | 2026-07-11 |
| `scripts/gen_cli_help.py` | `22efd71f10` | 2026-08-20 |

A joint "skip if either is missing" guard would have silenced the
`gen_cli_reference` check on every tree based in that five-week window, for no
reason. Two independent `if [ -f ... ]` blocks keep each check enforced exactly
as far back as its own script reaches.

The corroboration that settled it: `gen_cli_reference.py` is ALREADY gated with
this exact if-present shape in `.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml`, so
old-base trees already run and pass it there. A joint guard here would have
contradicted the treatment that script gets one directory over.

## The editable-install false alarm — worth knowing, written down nowhere else

My first probe showed the old tree's `gen_cli_reference.py --check` FAILING,
which if true would have meant the separate-guard decision reintroduced this
very bug for that script. It was an instrument artifact, not a tree property.

The worktree venv is an EDITABLE install, so `rebar` resolves from the CURRENT
`src/` regardless of which tree the script is invoked from. `PYTHONPATH` does
not fix it — the editable finder is a `sys.meta_path` entry, which is consulted
before the path finder. So the probe was running the OLD tree's generator
against the CURRENT package's help text, compared to the OLD tree's committed
docs: a guaranteed mismatch. Installing that tree's own rebar into a throwaway
venv and re-running gives exit 0 — the tree is self-consistent.

Real CI never has this problem, which is why the artifact is misleading rather
than merely noisy: the step runs `/tmp/clean/bin/python`, a venv holding a
wheel built from the SAME tree, so generator and package always agree.

Anyone probing a generator/drift gate from a worktree will hit this, and the
failure looks exactly like a genuine regression.
